title: console vite/vitest configs rely on features `configLoader: 'native'` drops — a future Vite major turns 5 warnings into a broken config load
body:
Found while working #3305 (wiring `apps/console/tsconfig.node.json` into a gate). **Not fixed there** — orthogonal to that change, filing per PD #10. Deliberately left unassigned.

## What

Every `vite build` / `vitest run` touching the console prints this, once per config load (so it repeats several times in one test run):

```
(!) Your Vite config uses features that are unsupported by `configLoader: 'native'`,
    which is planned to become the default in a future major version of Vite:
  - `__dirname` (vitest.config.ts:13:33). Use `import.meta.dirname` instead
  - import "./vite.config" without a file extension (vitest.config.ts:4:24). Add the file extension
  - `__dirname` (vite.config.ts:56:35). Use `import.meta.dirname` instead
  - import "../../scripts/vite-crypto-stub" without a file extension (vite.config.ts:6:32). Add the file extension
  - import "../../scripts/vite-maplibre-worker" without a file extension (vite.config.ts:7:36). Add the file extension
```

Two distinct incompatibilities, both in `apps/console`:

1. **`__dirname` in an ESM config** — `apps/console/vitest.config.ts` and `apps/console/vite.config.ts`. Vite's current (bundling) loader injects a CJS-ish shim; the native loader will not. Replacement is `import.meta.dirname`.
2. **Extensionless relative imports** — `vitest.config.ts` imports `./vite.config`, and `vite.config.ts` imports `../../scripts/vite-crypto-stub` / `../../scripts/vite-maplibre-worker`. Node's native ESM resolver does not do extension guessing.

(Line numbers above are from `origin/main`. On #3305's branch the two `scripts/` imports shift to 10/11 because a comment was added above them — the imports themselves are untouched.)

## Why it matters

This is dormant today — it is only a warning, and everything builds and tests green, which is why this is filed as a `finding` rather than a defect. What makes it worth recording is the failure mode when Vite flips the default: the console's config would fail to **load**, so `vite build`, `vite dev`, and the console's whole vitest project all die at once, on a dependency bump rather than on a code change. The fix is mechanical and can be done at any time; the cost of discovering it during an upgrade is a blocked upgrade.

There is also a mild interaction with #3305: `apps/console/tsconfig.node.json` now type-checks `vite.config.ts` **and** the `scripts/vite-*.ts` plugins, so whoever adds the file extensions has a gate that will confirm the specifiers still resolve. `moduleResolution: "bundler"` accepts both spellings, so adding `.ts` extensions there will not upset the type-check either way.

## Suggested direction (not decided)

- `__dirname` -> `import.meta.dirname` in both console configs.
- Add explicit extensions to the three relative config imports.
- Optionally set `configLoader: 'native'` explicitly afterwards so the repo pins the behaviour instead of waiting to inherit it, and any regression shows up immediately rather than at the next Vite major.
